_comment_canonical: CANONICAL in-tree PDHD TrackFitting configuration (pdhd/docs/stm-tagger-chain.md sec 4 for DL/DT, sec 5 for the transverse seeds). Consumed via the TaggerCheckSTM / TaggerCheckNeutrino 'trackfitting_config_file' knob. The path IS resolved through WIRECELL_PATH (Persist::resolve, TaggerCheckSTM.cxx load_trackfitting_config), so 'pgrapher/experiment/pdhd/pdhd_track_fitting.json' works; an absolute path passes through unchanged. (sbnd_track_fitting.json's claim that the path is NOT resolved is stale -- the resolve was added for PDVD and applies to every detector.) Keys starting with '_' are skipped by load_trackfitting_config. Values are WCT internal units (mm, us; cm^2/s = 1e-7). Read at RUNTIME: a byte-identical compiled jsonnet does NOT mean the fit is unchanged.
_comment: Forked BY DUPLICATION from protodunevd/pdvd_track_fitting.json (itself forked from sbnd/sbnd_track_fitting.json); both source files are untouched. Only the six detector keys differ (DL, DT, add_sigma_L, ind_sigma_u_T, ind_sigma_v_T, col_sigma_w_T) -- the uBooNE->SBND->PDVD porting surface. Everything else (selection knobs, min_drift_time floor 50 us, div_sigma, skip_revert_iso_xext_cut) is inherited unchanged.
_comment_diffusion: PHYSICAL PDHD transport coefficients from the BNL LAr-properties parameterisation (lar.bnl.gov/properties; pdhd/stm/pdhd_transport.py) at the field the CALIBRATED drift velocity implies: v = 1.576 mm/us (params.jsonnet lar.drift_speed and clus.jsonnet's local drift_speed, which agree -- unlike PDVD, doc pdvd/29 sec 3) inverted at T = 87.68 K (dunecore protodunehd_detproperties) gives E = 0.4959 kV/cm -> DL = 4.1207 cm^2/s, DT = 8.2017 cm^2/s (4.1207e-7 / 8.2017e-7 internal). The dunecore NOMINAL field is 0.4867 kV/cm (v_bnl = 1.5612 mm/us), so the calibration sits ~1 % high in velocity and ~1.9 % high in field; the LArSoft Walkowiak/ICARUS branch inverts the same velocity to 0.4942 kV/cm, a 0.3 % spread. T-band systematic: at 87.3 K the same velocity gives E = 0.4895, DL 4.129, DT 8.177 (<0.4 % on DT). PDHD runs on DATA in this chain, so the physical values apply; cfg/pgrapher/experiment/pdhd/params.jsonnet still inherits the GENERIC base defaults DL 7.2 / DT 12.0 cm^2/s / lifetime 8 ms (pgrapher/common/params.jsonnet) which the PDHD SIMULATION consumes through pgrapher/common/sim/nodes.jsonnet -- reconciling those is a separate owner decision (it would move every PDHD sim job's compiled config) and is NOT done here.
_comment_transverse_smearing: SEED VALUES, NOT A DERIVATION. ind_sigma_u_T / ind_sigma_v_T / col_sigma_w_T are the historical SP closed form (1/sqrt(pi)/Wire_ind 0.75) * 4.6693 mm U/V pitch * {0.3 U, 0.5 V} and (1/sqrt(pi)/Wire_col 10.0) * 4.7920 mm W pitch * 0.2, from cfg/pgrapher/experiment/pdhd/sp-filters.jsonnet -- the same formula that produced SBND's and PDVD's starting values. That closed form is WITHDRAWN as a derivation (doc pdvd/42 sec 8.2/8.6/8.10, doc pdvd/44): these keys are structurally the ENTIRE non-diffusion transverse width of the charge the fit is compared to, not the filter term, and on PDVD the closed form was 8-10x too small. It is used here only to give PDHD a defined starting point for the first STM-fit arm; the measured effective width replaces it. NOTE the ordering: PDHD's induction wire filter is the WIDEST of the three detectors in wire space (true Gaussian sigma 0.376 pitch = 1.756 mm, vs SBND 0.269 pitch = 0.806 mm and PDVD 0.056 pitch = 0.432 mm), so the seed is already at SBND's MEASURED level on U/V; the collection seed (0.054 mm) is as small as PDVD's was. Re-derive with pdhd/docs/scripts/d44_sigma_fit.py --det pdhd on a tracking-stm.root arm; NEVER re-derive from the SP filter closed form.
_comment_longitudinal: add_sigma_L = 1/(2*pi*Gaus_wide 0.12 MHz) * drift 1.576 mm/us = 1.32629 us * 1.576 = 2.0902 mm. Gaus_wide is the one SP time filter OmnibusSigProc consumes (Gaus_tight is dead config); PDHD's 0.12 MHz equals PDVD's. The drift speed here must be the one the grouping is configured with (TrackFitting reads it per (apa,face) from the grouping): the PR job must see params.jsonnet's 1.576 mm/us. PDHD sets ONE global drift speed, so unlike PDVD there is no per-crate hazard.
_comment_skip_revert_iso_xext_cut: doc pr/28 sec 17 round 10 (toolkit 6b219d14). C++ default -1 (off, unconditional revert). 200.0 = 20 cm (units::cm=10) -- SBND production default since 2026-08-06, inherited unchanged by PDVD and here by PDHD. Abstains from skip_trajectory_point's charge-consistency revert when the point's cluster has blob-center drift-x extent below this cut, i.e. isochronous clusters only.
